items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: We used to call them the Uncle Tom or the handkerchief head type of performer; that's all the parts they wrote for them.

ctx.x: I was thinking it was about time. But I'm so thrilled to know this because you have lent so much class to it, like we mentioned before, being the first black in an interracial band and being able to perform and carry that dignity, maintain that -- great people like you --

That is a serious problem. A lot of performers, Negro performers in the past -- I've sat in on meetings on this question where I've heard, actually, some of the people who've made some movies years ago, that if they don't behave that way -- that's the parts they write for them and if they don't behave that way, they're not going to get the job. We used to call them the Uncle Tom or the handkerchief head type of performer; that's all the parts they wrote for them.
I think the first Negro presented with any kind of dignity at all might have been -- what was that girl's name?
